scene.placeText: her lantern workshop at the open front of a covered bazaar lane in the old city of her steam city at dusk — a worn workbench of polished wood scattered with brass sheets, little punches and pieces of coloured glass, hundreds of finished star-pierced brass lanterns glowing overhead in ruby, emerald and amber, a carved wooden lattice balcony leaning over the lane and gas lamps coming on
scene.ownProp: a small brass lantern with a pointed domed cap, its sides pierced with stars and set with ruby, emerald and amber glass
scene.outfit: a lantern-maker look fitted to her body — a cropped Nile-blue waistcoat with polished brass buttons and a short shoulder cape of openwork brass lattice, a fitted brass-buckled waist band, a short skirt, fingerless leather gloves, brass goggles pushed up in her hair and laced ankle boots
scene.scene: she is the lane's lantern-maker, leaning over her workbench and fitting a last pane of ruby glass into a star-pierced brass lantern with both hands, its little flame just lit inside

prompt:

She is strikingly beautiful and refined — harmonious features, clear luminous skin, graceful posture — while her own face stays distinct: her face shape, eyes, brows, nose and lips follow the attached image, not a generic pretty face.

This is her world's own everyday life, not our present day: every made thing around her — tools, cups, lamps, signs, vehicles, money and devices — is made the way her world makes them.
